advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Emit a gate_error record on the completion gate's mid-run LLMUnavailableError path (wrap run_workflow), matching the plan/code-review mid-run capture, or document why completion intentionally captures only preflight.
evidence: gate_dispatch.py:671-678: completion wraps only `runner_sel.preflight()` in try/except LLMUnavailableError → emit_gate_error + raise
gate_dispatch.py:690-698: `with gate_config(cfg): res = _ex.run_workflow(...)` has NO try/except LLMUnavailableError around the mid-run call
gate_dispatch.py:181-187: plan-review DOES emit_gate_error on the mid-run except LLMUnavailableError path
gate_dispatch.py:622-629: code-review DOES emit_gate_error on the mid-run except LLMUnavailableError path
advisory.finding: The completion gate only wraps runner_sel.preflight() with gate_error emission; the mid-run run_workflow call is not wrapped, so a mid-run LLMUnavailableError in completion re-raises WITHOUT persisting a gate_error record — an asymmetry vs plan-review/code-review, which both capture the preflight AND the mid-run outage.
scenarios: Runner preflight passes but the LLM tier fails mid-run during completion verification with LLMUnavailableError

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for produce_code_review_verdict under an infra outage: assert a gate_error_v1 record is written on REVIEW_RESULT when target_ticket is set, and NOT written when target_ticket is None.
evidence: Source adds emit at gate_dispatch.py:546-549 `if request.target_ticket: emit_gate_error(request.target_ticket, "code_review", ...)` and again at :625-628

A regression that drops the `if request.target_ticket` guard, or emits under the wrong gate name, would not be caught
advisory.finding: The code_review gate's two new gate_error emit sites are entirely untested, including the `if request.target_ticket` guard branch — neither the positive (target_ticket set ⇒ record written) nor the negative (target_ticket None ⇒ no record) case has any regression coverage.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add two code_review cases (outage with target_ticket ⇒ record present; outage without target_ticket ⇒ no record), covering both the preflight and mid-run emit sites.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make emit_gate_error prune its host stream after append (as plan_review.sidecar.emit and completion_sidecar.emit do) so gate_error_v1 records are retention-bounded during a sustained outage.
evidence: gate_error_sidecar.py:71: `append_event(ticket_id, event_type, payload, tracker, repo_root=repo_root)` — no prune call follows
plan_review/sidecar.py:68: `prune(verdict.get("ticket_id", ""), repo_root=repo_root)  # best-effort retention`
completion_sidecar.py:59: `prune(str(verdict.get("ticket_id") or ""), repo_root=repo_root)  # best-effort retention`

completion_sidecar.py:36-39: COMPLETION_VERDICT is reducer-IGNORED and compaction PRESERVES it, so growth is only bounded by prune (RETAIN_PER_TICKET=10); REVIEW_RESULT likewise (RETAIN_PER_TICKET=50)

ABSENCE: during a prolonged outage no PASS/FAIL verdict emit occurs, so the peer prune that also matches `-COMPLETION_VERDICT.json`/`-REVIEW_RESULT.json` filenames never runs; gate_error records accumulate without bound
dropped.finding: emit_gate_error appends to the REVIEW_RESULT/COMPLETION_VERDICT streams but never prunes, unlike every peer sidecar emitter, so gate_error_v1 records grow unbounded during a sustained infra outage (no successful verdict emit runs to trigger the peer prune).
scenarios: A provider outage lasting many gate invocations on one ticket appends a gate_error_v1 record each time with no retention cap

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the reader-isolation test non-vacuous: assert latest is not None (or assert a positive plan_review_result_v1 was written) before asserting it is not the gate_error record.
evidence: test body: `latest = pr_sidecar.latest_review_result(...); if latest is not None: assert latest.get('schema') != 'gate_error_v1' ...`

_degraded_plan_review_verdict (gate_dispatch.py:402) returns a verdict but does not itself emit a plan_review_result sidecar; whether a plan_review_result_v1 record exists depends on review_plan's emit path, so latest may be None and the assertions skipped
If latest_review_result regressed to return the gate_error_v1 record only when no v1 record exists, the None-guarded assertions could still be skipped in this scenario, giving a false pass
dropped.finding: test_existing_verdict_readers_skip_gate_error_record guards its assertions behind `if latest is not None:`, so if latest_review_result returns None the test passes vacuously and asserts nothing — it is regression-blind to a reader that DOES surface the gate_error record when no normal review-result exists.
